That's exactly what a seiche is! It's one of the less well known tsunami effects. You have to have the right geography to get big ones. Unfortunately (especially in 1964), we do. Wind & atmospheric pressure can also cause seiche in the right circumstances. Lake Erie is prone to it:
Often driven by thunderstorms, meteotsunamis on the Great Lakes can be deadly and destructive. A buoy is collecting vital data to help understand -- and predict -- these rare events.
